title: Android Inc. and Google's Quiet 2005 Acquisition
explainer: Android began as Android Inc., a small startup founded in Palo Alto in October 2003 by Andy Rubin and Chris White, before Google quietly acquired it in July 2005 for at least $50 million without disclosing what it planned to build. The first commercial Android phone, the HTC Dream (T-Mobile G1), didn't ship until September 2008, five years after the company that started it all was founded - a reminder of how long a platform can incubate before its first public release.

title: Kotlin's Path From JetBrains Side Project to Android's Preferred Language
explainer: JetBrains, the company behind the IDE that Android Studio is built on, first unveiled Kotlin in July 2011 as an in-house JVM language project with no connection to Android at all. It took until Google I/O in May 2017, six years later, for Google to declare Kotlin a first-class, officially supported Android language, which is why so much pre-2017 Android code you'll encounter in the wild is still written in Java.
